level.name: AI-assisted
level.meaning: Models answer or draft inside the product; a person does the doing.

profile.title: Product
profile.meaning: Software people use directly; AI and automation serve the customer in the product.

criteria.label: API handlers a program can call
criteria.next: Expose the app's operations as API handlers; 20 or more earns the full ten.

criteria.label: A machine-readable API description
criteria.next: Publish an OpenAPI file or a GraphQL schema so an agent can read what exists without a person; the handlers you already have then count in full toward Reach. A capability inventory or typed contract schemas earn half.

criteria.label: Inbound webhooks from other systems
criteria.next: Receive events from the systems you depend on (payments, calendars, CRMs) with a signature check.

criteria.label: Work that runs on a schedule
criteria.next: Add scheduled jobs for the work a person currently remembers to do.

criteria.label: Queues or event pipelines
criteria.next: Put long or retried work on a queue or an event pipeline instead of a request.

criteria.label: A model provider integrated
criteria.next: Call a model from the server side; a second provider or a router earns the last two.

criteria.label: Prompts written down as code
criteria.next: Keep system prompts in files under version control, one per job.

criteria.label: Structured output the software acts on
criteria.next: Ask the model for a schema (JSON schema, zod, structured output) so its answer can drive code, not only a chat.

criteria.label: Retrieval over your own data
criteria.next: Embed your data and search it (pgvector or a vector store) so the model answers from your records.

criteria.label: Voice or vision
criteria.next: Add a voice or image path where your customers already speak or send pictures.

criteria.label: AI runs on the server, not only in the browser
criteria.next: Move model calls behind a server function so keys stay server-side and agents can call them too.

criteria.label: Tools a model may call
criteria.next: Define tools (functions with schemas) for the model; eight or more distinct tools earns the full nine.

criteria.label: A loop that lets the model act until done
criteria.next: Let the model call tools in a loop (maxSteps, tool_use handling, an agent runner) instead of one answer.

criteria.label: An MCP server exposing the software
criteria.next: Make the MCP server discoverable: declare the SDK, or publish a server card (.well-known/mcp/server-card.json) or mcp.json, and name the server in README or AGENTS.md. Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT find software the way this scanner does.

criteria.label: Orchestration or MCP client use
criteria.next: Chain steps in a workflow engine or graph, or consume other systems' MCP tools.

criteria.label: Memory kept between runs
criteria.next: Store threads, runs and agent memory in tables so work survives a restart and a second run knows the first.

criteria.label: Reach: machine surfaces against human pages
criteria.next: Every operation a person does in a page should be reachable by a handler or a tool; the ratio is what scores.

criteria.label: Machine surfaces that change things
criteria.next: Let handlers and tools write, not only read: create the record, send the thing, close the loop.

criteria.label: Observability of what ran
criteria.next: Trace and log every run (Sentry, Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, structured logs) so a failure is visible without a customer.

criteria.label: Retries, backoff, idempotency
criteria.next: Retry with backoff and make writes idempotent so an agent can safely try again.

criteria.label: Evals or tests of AI behaviour
criteria.next: Write evals for the prompts and tools; a change to a prompt should fail a test before it fails a customer.

criteria.label: Guardrails and a human gate
criteria.next: Rate limits and authenticated surfaces earn one; a human approval gate for the risky actions earns the other.

criteria.label: Documentation written for agents
criteria.next: Add AGENTS.md or llms.txt (and a server card for MCP) so an agent can learn the system without a person.

gate.rule: score 25 or more and level 1 Automated or above

evidence.what: API handlers (route files, serverless functions, framework routes)
Structured output (schemas the model must fill)
MCP server (the software's abilities offered to any agent), 1 written by hand (JSON-RPC initialize, tools/list, tools/call)

MCP server is not discoverable: no SDK declaration, no server card or mcp.json, no mention in README, AGENTS.md or llms.txt. Agents find software the way this scanner does; a surface they cannot find is one they cannot use
Memory and state kept between runs (threads, conversations, agent memory)
Reach: 6 handlers (undocumented, counted at a quarter) and 1 tools against 0 pages a person uses (ratio 1; 1 with a full API description)
Guardrails (rate limits 0, authenticated machine surfaces 5, moderation / redaction / cost caps 1)
Documentation written for agents (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, llms.txt, skills, server card)
